reply.subject: RM_Muttavaq

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Each shows a thick, flat, tan disc of clay plates with dark cracks running out from a central point, sitting on a dark brown, wrinkled hide body with short, flared, stumpy legs. South and north are about the same width and height. East is a long oval slab with the same radial cracks, three visible legs, and a tapered head end at the right with a mouth slit and a row of dark pits.
observed.south.png: Front view, slightly from above. A thick, slightly rounded clay slab whose cracks radiate from a central point. Along the front rim of the slab is a row of five small black pits. Under the rim is a shadowed horizontal mouth slit lined with fine teeth or bristles. Below that is a wrinkled, muscular brown underbody and four short, tapering, elephant-foot legs with flared pads. The slab is uniform tan with a fine speckled texture. The cutout is clean.
observed.east.png: Side profile. A long, low oval slab of cracked clay plates radiating from a center point, overhanging a folded brown hide body. Three stumpy flared legs are visible. At the right end the body narrows into a low snout with a long jaw slit with fine teeth, and five black pits sit on the rim above it. No left/right pose cue other than the head end. Clean cutout.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The same cracked radial clay slab and rim plates as south. Below it is a wrinkled hide underbody and four stumpy legs. There are no pits, mouth or eyes, and no tail. Width and height match south. Clean cutout.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the animal spans about 4 cells wide and is about 1.5 cells tall, against a human about 1 cell tall. At 32 px/cell it reads as a tan cracked disc on dark legs, several times the human's width: clearly a big creature. It stands apart from the ground as a pale top over a dark base.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head end: a row of sensory pits on the rim and a toothed mouth slit facing the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the slab and underbody only: no pits, mouth or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled game camera: the top surface is foreshortened and the rim and legs are visible below it.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured spread is 2%. In facings.png, south and north match in width and height.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same radial-crack slab, hide underbody and flared legs appear in all facings. The pits and mouth sit at the front end on south and east and are absent on north, so they turn with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: The clay-pan back with cracks radiating from a center is the dominant feature in every facing, and the jaw-plate mouth is visible on south and east. The pan reads as a thick slab more than a low mounded polygon field.

ALIEN.seen: Nobody would name it a tortoise at first glance: it has no shell dome, no tortoise head and no scutes. The cracked-pan back, sensory pits and straining mouth are present. The risk is that it reads as an object (a tabletop or pie) rather than as an Earth animal.

STYLE.seen: The hide folds and legs are painted with shaded volume, and the face is now a shadowed slit and pits, not a cartoon grin. The slab texture is a fine, even speckle that looks somewhat generated, but it is not cel-shaded or toy-like.

OURS.seen: A unique invented design. No vanilla or other-mod animal resembles it.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cutouts in every facing, with no ground patch or shadow; the code confirms real alpha.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The north size jump is fixed (2% spread), and the face is no longer cartoonish (shadowed slit and pits, no eyes or smile).

SCALE.seen: About 4 cells wide beside a 1-cell human, which fits a canyon-floor giant with drawSize 4.6. Arguably it could be larger for an animal people walk on unknowingly.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a pale cracked disc over a dark leggy base, distinct from the ground.

findings.where: all facings, mostly south and north
findings.seen: A thick, flat-edged slab with an even overhang, sitting on four evenly spaced stumpy legs. The overall silhouette is still a footstool or round tabletop (or a pie on legs), and the cut, vertical slab edge reads like a worked surface rather than a living back.
findings.quote: a natural thing that looks man-made
findings.fix: The back is a low, irregular dome of mounded clay polygons that slumps down into the hide at the edges with no straight cut rim, and the legs are splayed, uneven and partly hidden under the sagging hide, so the silhouette reads as a crouched animal bearing a dried mud crust.

findings.seen: The pan is a single smooth-topped slab of wedge plates, flat as a tray, rather than a low mounded polygon field of slightly raised cells.
findings.quote: a low mounded polygon field a touch too regular, cracks radiating from a center
findings.fix: Each clay polygon on the back is slightly domed and raised, giving a gently mounded, bumpy field cut by the radiating cracks.

findings.seen: A straight line of five evenly spaced round black dots above a horizontal mouth slit. At normal zoom this can still read as a simple face (dot eyes over a grin), and the drilled-looking pits are very regular.
findings.quote: Glossy round eyes and a smiling face are cute.
findings.fix: The sensory pits are irregular, recessed, moist openings of varied size, set in folds of hide under the rim near the jaw-plates, not a neat row of dots on the clay edge.

findings.seen: The clay plates carry a uniform, fine, noisy speckle with little painterly variation in light, so they look slightly like a generated texture next to the better-painted hide.
findings.quote: Painterly vanilla RimWorld: real anatomy… not a photo or a 3D render.
findings.fix: The clay plates are painted with broad strokes of warm light on the upper faces, cooler shade in the cracks and some dust and salt crust variation, matching the brushwork of the hide.

findings.seen: About 4 cells wide and 1.5 tall: large, but small for a pan described as terrain that people walk across.
findings.quote: walk THIS pan and you walk on one animal
findings.fix: The animal is drawn larger, about 5–6 cells across, to sell a terrain-sized giant.

reply.needs_call_why: Identity checks pass (facings, size, alpha, owner notes), but the silhouette is still a slab on four evenly spaced stubby legs, which may still read to the owner as a footstool or table (the CONSTRUCTED complaint from the previous judge run). The legs are now organic, so whether the remaining resemblance blocks or is polish is a judgment call.
proposals: When the defining feature is 'it is mistaken for terrain', add a checklist item asking whether the asleep or dug-in state reads as ground. That state is not covered by the walker facings.

reply.subject: RM_Muttavaq
reply.image_seen: The facing strip and individual south, east and north images show a broad, ochre cracked-clay back over a dark, folded body with tapering limbs; the scale panel shows a giant, low walking pan beside a human and rat.

concerns.evidence: South and north show bent, asymmetrical limbs merging into muscular shoulder folds and an uneven belly. East exposes overlapping, irregularly projecting rim plates. The broad overhang remains prominent, but its broken perimeter and organically attached limbs support the intended walking clay-pan anatomy.

All three facings show a shallow central rise, with the upper silhouette descending toward the perimeter. Branching cracks subdivide the radial sectors into irregular polygons, and individual perimeter cells have different heights and projections. This visibly supplies the description's low mounded polygon field.

South has five small, recessed pits spread across the rim rather than a bilateral pair of expressive eyes. East continues that sensory row along the forward edge. The mouth is a shadowed seam beneath the overhang, with no visibly upturned smiling corners; the normal-play inset reads as a dark underside beneath the pan.

The back contains visible irregular cream, ochre and brown painted patches. Plate edges darken and the upper surfaces brighten, while cracks carry deeper shadows. Its finer, angular texture contrasts with the broader hide folds in a way consistent with their different materials, and the normal-play inset retains coherent clay plates.
